title: The Quiet Machinery of Cities
body: Beneath every pavement there is a second city that almost no one sees. Water moves through cast-iron veins laid down in 1897, and fibre optic strands carry the weight of a morning's conversations. Maintenance is a form of memory. A city that forgets its pipes will eventually be reminded by them, usually at four in the morning and usually in winter.

title: Notes on Reading Speed
body: An average adult reads roughly 240 words per minute on paper and about 180 on a backlit screen. Comprehension falls by 12 to 15 percent once the pace exceeds 400 words per minute. The eye does not glide across a line. It jumps in short bursts called saccades, resting for 200 to 250 milliseconds at each stop. Meaning is assembled during those pauses.

title: A Letter from the Coast
body: Dear Miriam, the fog arrived on Tuesday and has not left since. I have started counting the days by the number of ships I cannot see. The lighthouse keeper says this is ordinary for October. I bought bread from the woman at the harbour who insists she remembers my grandfather. Perhaps she does. I have stopped correcting people about the past.

title: Quarterly Operations Summary
body: Total throughput for Q3 reached 1,482,600 units, an increase of 8.4% over Q2 and 21.7% year over year. Defect density fell to 0.032 per thousand, the lowest since 14 March 2019. Two constraints remain. Packaging capacity at Plant B is fixed at 6,000 units per shift, and the freight contract expires on 31 January.

title: On the Habit of Walking
body: Walking is the only exercise that doubles as thinking. The pace is slow enough to notice a doorway and fast enough to leave an argument behind. There is nothing mystical about it. Movement raises the pulse a little, and the mind, relieved of the duty to stare at a wall, begins to wander usefully.

title: Field Notes: Migratory Birds
body: Observed 09:40, clear sky, wind NNW at 11 km/h. A flock of roughly 60 barn swallows moving south along the ridge line. Two juveniles trailing by some 200 metres. The species winters as far as 9,000 kilometres from its breeding grounds. A bird ringed here in 2021 was recovered the following spring within 40 metres of the same barn.

title: The Repair Shop
body: Old Dessin never turned a customer away, though he was famous for telling them the truth about their belongings. The clock is not worth the repair, he would say, but it was your mother's, so I will do it anyway. His workbench held 400 tiny drawers, none of them labelled. He claimed the labels were in his hands.

title: Instructions for the New Kettle
body: 1. Remove all packaging and rinse the interior with clean water before first use. Do not immerse the base in water at any time. 2. Fill to a level between the MIN and MAX marks. Filling above MAX may cause boiling water to escape from the spout. 3. Place the kettle on the base and press the switch. The unit shuts off automatically at 100 °C. 4. Descale every three months. Use 250 ml of white vinegar and leave to stand for one hour.

title: A Short History of Paper
body: Paper reached Samarkand around 751, Baghdad by 793, and Fabriano in northern Italy by 1276, where water-powered hammers replaced hand pounding and turned a craft into an industry. For most of that history paper was made from rags, not trees. The switch to wood pulp in the 1840s made books cheap and, unfortunately, made them brittle.

title: Weather Log — 14 March
body: 06:00 −2 °C, frost on the north field, visibility approx. 300 m. Barometer 1013 hPa and rising slowly. 12:00 7 °C, cloud cover 4/8, wind SW 18 km/h gusting 30. The last of the frost gone by half past ten. 18:00 4 °C, light rain beginning, 3.2 mm recorded by nightfall. Barometer down to 1006 hPa. Note: the river gauge at the mill read 1.42 m, some 0.6 m above the seasonal average.

title: The Cartographer's Complaint
body: Every map is a lie told for a good reason. Flatten a sphere and something must tear; the only choice is where to put the wound. Greenland swells, Africa shrinks, and generations grow up with the wrong idea of scale. The honest cartographer states the projection in the corner and hopes somebody reads it.

title: Service Bulletin SB-4471
body: Affected units: serial numbers 88-2140 through 88-3390 manufactured between June 2022 and February 2023. A tolerance error in the seal housing may permit coolant seepage under sustained load. Action required within 90 days. Replace part no. 41-B/7 and torque to 24 N·m. Labour is covered under warranty; freight is not.

title: The Last Train
body: The 23:47 to Bridgeton carries a particular kind of passenger. Nobody on it is going anywhere important. The conductor has stopped pretending to check tickets and reads the same folded newspaper he has read since Tuesday. At Halford the doors open onto an empty platform. Nobody gets on. The doors close again, patiently, as if disappointed.

title: How Bread Fails
body: A dense loaf usually means the yeast was tired or the water too hot — above 46 °C will kill it outright. A loaf that collapses in the oven rose too long and ran out of structure. Salt is not optional. At roughly 2% of flour weight it slows fermentation and holds the crumb together. Forget it and you get a pale, fast, tasteless bread.

title: Minutes of the Parish Council
body: Present: Mrs. Halloway (chair), Mr. Ede, Dr. Simms, and four members of the public. Apologies received from Mr. Trant. Item 3: the churchyard wall. Two quotations were tabled, £4,200 and £5,850. The council resolved by 3 votes to 1 to seek a third before proceeding. Item 4 was deferred to the meeting of 12 November.

title: The Difficulty with Averages
body: If one person earns nothing and another earns £100,000, the average income is £50,000 and describes neither of them. The median is often kinder to the truth, but it hides the tails. Statistics do not lie so much as they simplify, and simplification is always a choice made by somebody with a purpose.

title: A Recipe for Lentil Soup
body: Sweat one large onion, two carrots and two sticks of celery in 2 tbsp olive oil for 8–10 minutes. Add 300 g of brown lentils, 1.2 litres of stock, and a bay leaf. Simmer 35 minutes until the lentils give way. Season at the end — salt added early keeps the skins tough. Finish with lemon juice, which matters more than it sounds.

title: On Losing Things
body: Keys are never lost in interesting places. They are found in the coat you wore on Thursday, in the bag you already searched twice, on the hook where they belong. The search itself is the punishment: fifteen minutes of increasingly unreasonable behaviour, ending in a discovery that makes the previous fourteen minutes look ridiculous.

title: Glacier Survey, Site 12
body: Terminus retreat measured at 47 m since the 2019 survey, an acceleration on the 31 m recorded over the preceding four years. Ice thickness at the central stake fell by 3.8 m. Meltwater discharge peaked at 14.2 m³/s on 3 August. Samples were drawn at 08:00 and 20:00 daily; sediment load remains under review.

title: The Rules of the House
body: No shoes past the hallway. No arguments at the table. Anyone who cooks does not wash up. The last person awake closes the shutters, and the first person awake opens them again. These were never written down. They were enforced by a look, which was more effective than any list would have been.

title: Concerning Fog
body: Fog is simply cloud that has lost its ambition. It forms when moist air cools to its dew point near the ground — often overnight, over water, or against a hillside. Radiation fog burns off by mid-morning. Advection fog, drifting in from a cold sea, can sit for days and cares nothing for the sun.

title: Interview Transcript, Extract 7
body: Q: You were on site the whole afternoon? A: From about half one until six, yes. Q: And you saw nothing unusual? A: I said I saw nothing. Whether it was unusual isn't for me to judge — I'd only been there three weeks and half the machines were new to me.

title: The Economics of Small Shops
body: A corner shop turning over £1,800 a week on a 22% gross margin makes £396 before rent, power, and the owner's time. Rent alone may be £250. The arithmetic is brutal and well understood by everyone who tries it. What keeps them open is rarely profit. It is the fact that somebody has to sell milk at seven in the morning.

title: Notes on Handwriting
body: Cursive was taught for speed, not beauty. A pen that never leaves the page moves faster than one that lifts between letters — a real advantage when documents were copied by hand. Ballpoints changed the geometry. They need pressure and dislike sharp turns, which is roughly when handwriting began its long decline into the illegible.

title: The Tenant's Notice
body: In accordance with clause 14(b) of the agreement dated 1 April 2023, the tenant hereby gives one calendar month's notice to terminate, such notice to expire on 31 May. The deposit of £950 is held under scheme reference DPS-77401-K and should be returned within ten working days of the final inspection.

title: Why Ships Are Slow
body: A container vessel cruises at about 20 knots, roughly 37 km/h — slower than a suburban bus. Fuel consumption rises with the cube of speed, so a modest slowdown saves an immodest amount of oil. After 2008 the industry adopted "slow steaming" almost overnight. It was framed as an environmental measure. It was, first of all, arithmetic.

title: The Museum at Closing Time
body: At ten to six the guards begin their slow migration inward, herding the last visitors toward the atrium the way water is drawn to a drain. Nobody is asked to leave; everybody leaves. The paintings spend twenty-two hours a day unobserved. It is difficult not to wonder whether that is a loss to them or a relief.

title: Standard Operating Procedure 3.2
body: Before opening the enclosure, confirm that the isolator is locked out and tagged. Verify absence of voltage on all three phases using an instrument tested immediately before and after the check. Record the reading in the log (Form E-19). Do not proceed if any phase reads above 5 V. Escalate to the duty engineer on ext. 2244.

title: A Theory of Queues
body: The other line does move faster, on average, and this is not paranoia. If there are three lines and yours is chosen at random, there is a two-in-three chance that a faster one exists. Single-queue systems eliminate the injustice entirely, which is why banks adopted them and supermarkets, for reasons of floor space, did not.

title: The Orchard in February
body: Pruning looks like violence to anyone who has not done it. A third of last year's growth comes off, sometimes more, and the tree stands in the cold looking robbed. By August the argument is settled. Light reaches the inner branches, the fruit is larger, and the wood that was cut would have carried nothing worth carrying.

title: Product Recall Notice
body: Model KX-220 travel adapters sold between 12 May and 30 September may present a shock hazard due to inadequate pin insulation. Approximately 24,000 units are affected across seven markets. Customers should stop using the product immediately and contact recall@example-support.com or telephone 0800 118 4400 for a full refund. Proof of purchase is not required.

title: On Reading in Translation
body: A translator makes ten thousand small betrayals in the service of one large loyalty. Rhythm is sacrificed for sense, or sense for rhythm, and the reader never learns which. The naïve complaint is that something is lost. Of course it is. The alternative is a book you cannot read at all.

title: Bridge Inspection Report
body: Span 4 shows longitudinal cracking on the soffit, maximum width 0.4 mm, consistent with earlier observations from 2021. No change in deflection was recorded under test load. Bearing at pier 3 exhibits corrosion and restricted movement; replacement is recommended within 24 months. Estimated cost £310,000. Traffic management would require single-lane closure for six weeks.

title: The Coffee Argument
body: Water at 93 °C, a dose of 18 g, a yield of 36 g in 28 seconds — the numbers are recited like scripture in every café with a wooden counter. They are useful, and they are not the point. The same machine in two hands makes two drinks. What the numbers describe is a starting position, not a result.

title: A Note Left on the Table
body: Gone to the market. Back by twelve. The plumber is coming at eleven — the stopcock is under the stairs, behind the box of Christmas things you said you would throw away in March. There is soup. Please do not put the good pan in the dishwasher again. P.

title: Frequencies and Interference
body: Wi-Fi at 2.4 GHz reaches further and penetrates walls better; at 5 GHz it is faster and less crowded. Microwave ovens, baby monitors and older cordless phones all shout in the 2.4 band. If the connection degrades every evening at seven, the cause is rarely the router. It is the neighbours, all forty of them, coming home.

title: The Auctioneer's Rhythm
body: Lot 214, a mahogany writing desk, circa 1830, with two later handles. We'll start at three hundred. Three-fifty, four hundred, four-fifty in the room, five hundred with the telephone. Five-fifty. Any advance on five-fifty? Fair warning. Sold, at £550, to the gentleman at the back — number 47, thank you.

title: Sleep and the Clock
body: The body runs on a cycle of roughly 24.2 hours and is corrected daily by morning light. Deny it that light and the whole schedule drifts later, a few minutes at a time. This is why shift work is punishing and why teenagers are not lazy. Their internal clock genuinely runs late, by about two hours, and no amount of shouting adjusts it.

title: The Village Store, 1962
body: Everything was weighed. Sugar into blue paper bags, tea from a tin with a dented lid, biscuits by the quarter-pound from a glass case with a chipped corner. Nothing had a barcode and everything had a price the shopkeeper carried in her head. She was wrong perhaps twice a year, and always in the customer's favour.

title: Concerning Rust
body: Iron returns to the state it was found in. Given oxygen and water it becomes iron oxide, expanding as it goes — which is why rust lifts paint and splits the metal beneath it. Everything we build from steel is on loan. Paint, galvanising and cathodic protection buy time; none of them cancel the debt.

title: Trial Balance, 31 December
body: Debits: cash at bank 12,480; trade receivables 33,215; inventory 21,900; equipment at cost 84,000. Credits: trade payables 19,640; accrued expenses 4,315; loan (due 2027) 45,000. Depreciation of 8,400 has not yet been posted. The suspense account of 1,275 must be cleared before the accounts are finalised.

title: The Long Way Round
body: He always took the coast road, which added eleven miles and twenty-five minutes to a journey he made four times a week. His wife pointed this out for eleven years. After the funeral his son drove the coast road once, on a grey Tuesday, and understood the argument entirely without being able to explain it to anyone.

title: Notes on Public Speaking
body: The audience wants you to succeed. This is the single most useful fact available to a nervous speaker, and it is almost never believed at the time. Speak slower than feels natural, pause where you would rather rush, and remember that a silence which feels endless from the front lasts about two seconds from the fourth row.

title: The Reservoir
body: In the dry summer of 1976 the water fell far enough to expose the village they had flooded in 1935 — a bridge, a lane, and the footings of eleven houses. People came from three counties to walk in it. Within a fortnight the rain returned, and the place went back under, having been visible for nineteen days.

title: On Choosing a Font
body: Legibility is measured at a glance; readability is measured over a page. A face can be excellent at one and exhausting at the other, which is why road signs and novels look nothing alike. x-height, counter size and stroke contrast do most of the work. Everything else is taste, and taste should be argued about after the text has been read.

title: Emergency Procedure — Vessel 2
body: In the event of overpressure, the relief valve lifts at 8.5 bar and vents to the roof stack. Do not attempt to isolate a lifting valve. Evacuate to muster point C, west of the weighbridge. Roll call is taken by the shift supervisor. Do not re-enter the building until the all-clear is given verbally, not by alarm.

title: Two Kinds of Silence
body: There is the silence of a library, which is full of held breath and turning pages, and there is the silence of a moor in November, which is not empty either but is indifferent. People who claim to like silence usually mean the first. Very few are comfortable for long with the second.

title: The Cost of Free Delivery
body: Nothing ships for nothing. A £3.90 delivery charge removed from the basket reappears in the unit price, in the minimum order value, or in the annual membership. The change is not deception so much as psychology: shoppers abandon carts over a visible fee and accept an invisible one without complaint.

title: Learning an Instrument at Forty
body: The hands are slower and the ear is better. A child practises by repetition and an adult by diagnosis, which is more efficient and considerably less fun. Progress arrives in plateaus. Six weeks of nothing, then one afternoon the passage plays itself and you cannot say what changed.

title: Soil Analysis, Field 6
body: pH 6.2, slightly acidic. Organic matter 4.1%, up from 3.3% following two seasons of cover cropping. Phosphorus index 2, potassium index 2−. Recommendation: apply 60 kg/ha of nitrogen in split doses, the first in late March. Lime is not required this season. Re-test in autumn 2027.

title: The Night Shift
body: Between two and four the hospital changes character. The corridors keep their lights but lose their traffic, and the sounds separate — a trolley three wards away, a lift settling, someone coughing behind a curtain. Nurses call it the low tide. It is when the sickest patients decline and when, occasionally, they turn a corner nobody expected.

title: Concerning Locks
body: A lock is a delay, not a barrier. The industry rates them in minutes: a cylinder certified to resist attack for five minutes is considered good, and ten is considered excellent. Most burglaries do not involve the lock at all. They involve a window left open, a key under a pot, or a door that was never actually pulled shut.

title: Shipping Manifest 09-A
body: Container MSKU 447 219-3, sealed 06:15, gross weight 21,340 kg. Contents: 480 cartons of ceramic tile, HS code 6907.21, origin Portugal. Discrepancy noted on arrival: 478 cartons landed, 2 damaged beyond inspection. Claim raised under policy MRN-2024/8812. Photographs attached at annex B.

title: The Grammar of Signage
body: Airports speak a stripped language: BAGGAGE RECLAIM, GATES 40–68, NOTHING TO DECLARE. No verbs, no politeness, no ambiguity — a syntax designed to survive exhaustion and poor eyesight. It works because it assumes nothing about the reader except that they are tired and in a hurry, which is a safe assumption at three in the morning.

title: How a Match Works
body: The head holds an oxidiser and a fuel; the striking surface holds red phosphorus and powdered glass. Friction converts a little phosphorus to white, which ignites in air at about 34 °C. The whole event takes under a second and was, for most of human history, an impossible luxury.

title: A Complaint to the Council
body: I write regarding the streetlight outside 14 Alder Row, which has failed intermittently since 3 June. It was reported by telephone on 7 June (ref. 22-11840) and again online on 19 June. The road is used by schoolchildren from 08:10 each weekday. I would be grateful for a firm date for repair rather than a further acknowledgement of receipt.

title: The Second Coat
body: Painters know the first coat is a lie. It looks finished under the wrong light and disappoints by morning, when every edge shows through and the colour reads thin. The second coat costs another afternoon and is the entire difference between a job done and a job done again next spring.

title: Numbers in the Wild
body: Written figures collide badly with speech. Nobody says "one thousand four hundred and eighty-two"; they say "about fifteen hundred", and the precision was never load-bearing. Reports that insist on 1,482.37 when 1,500 would do are not being accurate. They are being defensive.

title: The Tide Table
body: High water at Ferryside: 04:52 (5.9 m) and 17:14 (6.1 m). Low water: 11:03 (0.8 m) and 23:29 (0.6 m). Times are GMT; add one hour from 30 March. The causeway is passable roughly two hours either side of low water. Vehicles have been lost by people who rounded that figure up.

title: On Apologies
body: "I'm sorry you feel that way" is not an apology; it is a diagnosis. A real one names the act, accepts the effect, and offers something different next time. It is also short. Length in an apology is usually the sound of someone building a case.

title: The Wire Fence
body: It took eight days to fence the top field: 640 metres of line, 41 posts, three strainers and a gate that had to be hung twice because the ground had other ideas. The sheep tested it within an hour of completion, found one weak point at post 19, and were through it by supper.

title: Concerning Echoes
body: Sound travels about 343 m/s in dry air at 20 °C. For an echo to be heard as separate from the original, the reflecting surface must be at least 17 metres away. Closer than that and the return arrives too soon to be distinguished; it is heard instead as reverberation, which is what makes a small tiled room sound larger than it is.

title: The Understudy
body: She had learned the part for eleven weeks and performed it never, which is the ordinary condition of the job. Each evening she dressed, waited, and went home. On the Thursday it happened, she was told at 19:12 for a 19:30 curtain. She said afterwards that the only unfamiliar thing was the applause.

title: Insurance Schedule — Summary
body: Buildings sum insured: £480,000. Contents: £60,000. Excess: £350 (standard), £1,000 (subsidence, escape of water). Cover excludes damage arising from gradual deterioration, faulty workmanship, and any loss occurring while the property is unoccupied for more than 45 consecutive days.

title: The Nine O'Clock Bell
body: The foundry bell rang at nine, at one, and at five-thirty for a hundred and six years, and the town set its clocks by it long after everyone had wristwatches. When the works closed in 1991 the silence was reported to the council as a fault. Three separate residents called to say something was wrong.

title: Reading a Nutrition Label
body: Per 100 g is the only figure that permits comparison; per serving is a number chosen by the manufacturer. A "serving" of cereal is often 30 g, which is less than anyone pours. Ingredients are listed by weight, descending. If sugar appears in the first three, the front of the packet is describing a different product from the back.

title: The Ferry in Winter
body: Sailings are weather-dependent from November. In practice this means the 07:00 goes, the 12:30 is doubtful, and the 17:45 is a matter of opinion held by one man in a hut. Islanders plan around it without complaint. Visitors argue with the timetable as though it were a contract.

title: Notes on Estimating
body: Ask how long a task will take and you will be told the duration of the work. You will not be told the waiting, the mistakes, or the day lost to a delivery that arrives without its fittings. The old rule is to double the estimate and move to the next unit: a two-hour job becomes four days. It is a joke that survives because it is frequently correct.

title: The Rented Room
body: Third floor, one window, a wardrobe that did not open fully because of the door. The rent was £62 a week and included a bathroom shared with a man who worked nights and was therefore theoretical. It was the smallest place I have ever lived and the only one I can still draw from memory, wall by wall.

title: Concerning Salt
body: Salt was taxed, traded and fought over because it was the only reliable way to keep meat and fish through winter. Roads were built to move it; cities grew where it was found. Refrigeration made it ordinary in about forty years. We now spend more effort avoiding it than our ancestors spent obtaining it.

title: Access Log Extract
body: 2026-02-11 14:03:22 — badge 4471 granted, door W2. 14:03:41 — badge 4471 granted, door W5. 14:11:09 — badge 4471 denied, door SRV-1 (insufficient privilege). Three further denials followed within ninety seconds from the same badge. Security was notified at 14:19 and the card was suspended pending review.

title: The Photograph
body: Four people on a beach, squinting, one of them mid-sentence. On the back, in pencil: "Filey, Aug '58" and three names, the fourth having been forgotten by whoever wrote it. That fourth person stands closest to the camera and is the only one laughing. Nobody now living can say who she was.

title: How Bicycles Stay Upright
body: Not by gyroscopic force, whatever the textbooks used to claim. Researchers built a bicycle with counter-rotating wheels to cancel that effect and it balanced perfectly well. The real mechanism is steering. A falling bicycle steers into the fall, moving the wheels back under the centre of mass — a correction the rider makes constantly and cannot describe.

title: Terms of Engagement
body: Fees are charged at £145 per hour, billed monthly in arrears, with disbursements at cost. An initial retainer of £1,500 is payable on instruction. Estimates are given in good faith and are not caps. Where a matter is likely to exceed the estimate by more than 15%, we will notify you in writing before the additional work is undertaken.

title: The Allotment
body: Plot 31 was neglected for six years and produced, in its first restored season, four courgettes and an unreasonable quantity of nettles. In the second it produced enough to give away. Nobody there discusses anything but soil, rain, and the shortcomings of the water committee. It is the most restful conversation available in the borough.

title: Concerning Anaesthesia
body: We do not fully know how general anaesthetics work. We know the dose, the effect, and the recovery curve, and we have used them safely for over a century without a complete mechanism. Consciousness switches off in under thirty seconds and returns with no experience of the interval — not sleep, not darkness, simply a missing piece.

title: The Wrong Address
body: For two years the flat received letters for a Mr. D. Okonkwo: bank statements, a jury summons, and finally a card that read only "we miss you, please call". I wrote "not at this address" on the first hundred. On the last one I did not, and I have thought about that more often than is reasonable.

title: Load Testing Results
body: At 500 concurrent users, median response time was 240 ms and the 95th percentile 610 ms. At 1,000 users the median held at 265 ms but the 95th percentile rose sharply to 2.4 s. The bottleneck was traced to connection pool exhaustion (max 40). Raising the pool to 120 flattened the curve to 380 ms at the 95th percentile.

title: On Being Early
body: The chronically early are not organised; they are anxious. They have simply chosen to spend the discomfort in advance, in a car park, rather than on the road. It buys a genuine advantage — the calm of arriving before you are needed — at the price of several hundred wasted hours a year.

title: The Bell Foundry
body: A bell is tuned by removing metal from the inside, never the outside, on a vertical lathe. Five separate tones must be brought into agreement: hum, prime, tierce, quint and nominal. Take away too much and there is no correcting it. The bell is broken up and the metal, at least, goes back into the furnace.

title: Directions to the House
body: Leave the A38 at junction 6 and take the second exit signposted Hensfield. After 1.4 miles turn left at the postbox — not at the first lane, which looks more like a road and is not. Continue past the barn conversion. The track is unmade for 300 m. If you reach the ford you have gone too far by about half a mile.

title: Concerning Applause
body: Clapping synchronises without instruction. Within seconds a crowd of two thousand finds a common rhythm, holds it, dissolves into noise, and finds it again. No one leads and no one follows deliberately. It is one of the few things a large group of strangers can do together perfectly on the first attempt.

title: The Locksmith's Ledger
body: March 14 — 3 Cotton Street, front door, cylinder replaced, £68. March 15 — Grange Motors, safe, combination reset, £120. March 15 — 9 Vale Rise, lock-out, entry gained without damage, £85. March 16 — no calls. March 17 — 9 Vale Rise again, same customer, same reason. Charged £60 and gave her a spare key for nothing.

title: Why Ice Floats
body: Water expands by about 9% as it freezes, which makes ice less dense than the liquid it came from. Almost nothing else behaves this way. The consequence is that lakes freeze from the top down and life continues beneath. Had water behaved conventionally, they would freeze solid from the bed upward, and the world would be a different place entirely.

title: Notes Left in a Library Book
body: Page 41: "he never says this to her directly!!" Page 88: a shopping list — eggs, capers, string. Page 203: "ask Dr. Beale about this chapter". The book was returned in 2009 and borrowed eleven times since. Nobody has removed the notes, which now read as a second, shorter book about someone else's semester.

title: Depreciation Schedule
body: Vehicles: 25% reducing balance. Plant and machinery: straight line over 8 years. Fixtures: straight line over 10 years. Computer equipment: straight line over 3 years. Assets acquired mid-year are charged a full year's depreciation in the year of purchase and none in the year of disposal. This policy is unchanged since 2018.

title: The Weight of Rain
body: A millimetre of rain across one hectare is ten tonnes of water. The 3.2 mm that fell on Tuesday put roughly 32 tonnes on the top field and moved a good deal of it downhill. Farmers do not experience weather as a forecast. They experience it as a mass arriving on a slope.

title: On Naming Things
body: In programming, the hardest problems are said to be cache invalidation and naming things. The joke survives because the second half is true and unglamorous. A badly named variable is a small lie that every future reader must first detect and then forgive. There are files in production carrying names that stopped being accurate in 2014.

title: The Cellar Steps
body: Eleven steps down, worn in the centre by three centuries of the same descent, and cold from the fourth step onward regardless of the season. The house has been rewired, replumbed and reroofed. Nobody has touched the steps, and nobody has suggested it.

title: Concerning Compound Interest
body: £100 at 5% becomes £105 in a year and £162.89 in ten, because interest earns interest. Reverse the sign and the same arithmetic governs debt with equal patience. The rule of 72 is close enough for mental use: divide 72 by the rate to get the doubling time. At 6%, twelve years. At 12%, six.

title: Safety Data — Section 4
body: After inhalation: move to fresh air. If breathing is difficult, give oxygen and seek medical attention. After skin contact: wash with soap and water for at least 15 minutes. After eye contact: rinse cautiously with water for several minutes; remove contact lenses if present and easy to do. Do NOT induce vomiting after ingestion.

title: The Border Town
body: The line runs through the middle of Kirkstead: the pub is in one country, its car park in another, and the difference is worth about 14 pence on a litre of fuel. Everyone drives the extra half mile. Nobody thinks of it as remarkable, and children raised there are astonished to learn that most borders are somewhere else.

title: On Rewriting
body: The first draft exists to be wrong in a useful direction. It converts a vague intention into a specific mistake, which is the only thing that can be corrected. Writers who cannot bear to be wrong on paper produce very little, very slowly, and it is rarely better.

title: Maintenance Log — Pump 3
body: 12 Jan: bearing noise reported, grease applied, monitoring. 04 Feb: noise persists, vibration reading 7.2 mm/s (alarm 8.0). 21 Feb: reading 8.9 mm/s, pump taken offline. 24 Feb: bearing replaced (part 6208-2RS), alignment checked with laser, reading after restart 2.1 mm/s. Next inspection due 24 Aug.

title: The Uses of Boredom
body: Children who are never bored never learn what to do about it, and what to do about it is most of invention. The empty afternoon is not a failure of scheduling. Adults have solved boredom entirely, which is why so few of us can now sit in a waiting room without reaching for something.

title: Concerning Sourdough
body: The starter is a stable culture of wild yeast and lactic acid bacteria, fed on flour and water, and it is considerably harder to kill than most people fear. Neglected for a month in the fridge it will sulk, separate, and smell of acetone. Two feedings at 1:5:5 by weight and it is generally back in business.

title: The Last Page of the Diary
body: Nothing much today. Rain until three. Wrote to Edward. The garden needs doing and I have not done it, and I will say the same tomorrow. The entry is dated 4 October 1974 and the remaining eighty-eight pages are blank. She lived, records show, until 1991.

title: How Escalators Fail
body: Rarely dramatically. The usual fault is a worn step chain, detected by a jolt at the comb plate that regular users notice weeks before it is reported. A stopped escalator is stairs, which is why the sign says TEMPORARILY OUT OF SERVICE rather than the more honest DO NOT PANIC, IT IS STILL A STAIRCASE.

title: Terms of Reference
body: The review shall examine decisions taken between 1 May 2024 and 30 April 2025, the information available to those taking them, and the adequacy of the procedures then in force. It shall not determine individual liability. Findings are due within six months; an interim note is expected by week 12. All staff are directed to cooperate fully.

title: The End of the Season
body: The deckchairs are stacked by the fourth week of September and the kiosk shutters come down with a sound the whole promenade can hear. The gulls stay on out of habit. For eight months the town belongs to about nine hundred people, which is the number that actually lives there, and the arithmetic of summer stops making sense to anyone.
